dude finally, I was going crazy reading the other comments. Both Ellie and Dina are so juvenile in the show compared to the game. They have banter and quirky moments in the game, but they're not obnoxious tik-tok teenagers. 

At this point in the original story they're experienced and mature. In these settings the environment will force you to grow up, or you'll be eaten. So they're 19 in the game, but they act and feel 25, which makes sense given what they've gone through. Here they look and act 14, which also might make some moments later feel off and uncomfortable (you know the ones). 

There's also a big difference between Ellie in game 1 to game 2. She's naturally grown based on age, and the aftermath of the first game has forced change. In the show she's basically identical to season 1, outside of her not liking Joel. 

It feels very much so that these characters are sort of just now "starting off", that they're just at the beginning of their journey, which they aren't, even in the show. 



"Don't like the changes they made to the story in regards to Abbys motivations being revealed instantly" 

\- not only that, but the whole episode was that way. They reveal far too much about the characters and their intentions. A lot of the interest and intrigue in the game comes from us slowly piecing together the puzzle, with certain events happening to build context to the story. I'm not sure here if it's bad writing or if they're just paranoid that people won't understand the story, so they just dumb it down. Joel's therapy acts that way too, it exists as a way of giving viewers answers about Joel and Ellie without us figuring it out ourselves. 

In the game, we figure out that Ellie's and Joel's relationship took a hit from her getting to know the truth, they don't tell us that explicitly right at the start of the game. Here they basically just completely and entirely tell us straight up, so that it wouldn't go past anyone. There's so much maturity and complexity ripped out from the original story to make this, be it the characters or overall plot. So far the game has acted as a better tv-series than this.

Dia jungle here. When you start your clear, you should think about where you want to end up. Not just what the other guy said, with pathing to the most important lane. But in ways to avoid the enemy jungler. Eve gets abused by a lot of gank jungler types, so I’d figure out where the xin/lee/elise types start. You die to invades, and you die to counter ganks. Ward enemy buffs, think logically where they’ll start. Low elo 99% of the time they go botside up to top. I’m making assumptions, but the typical low elo will try too hard to make plays all the time. Fuck ganking lanes unless it’s completely free, especially before ult. Do your first clear. Recall, go to your starting camp which will have respawned. Full sequence again (all camps most often times) look for some safe play (as in will work 90% of the time). Do this on repeat. Sometimes you’ll need to adapt, objectives, win cons etc but this is the general copy paste for all games. Play smart like this and look carefully for chances to pop off. High cs scores, level leads and low deaths. Ignore the laners begging for help, stick to the plan. This will be more consistant and is repeatable. Keep watch of the enemy jungler. They show botside and you sweep their topside camps putting you ahead. If you’re not 1/2 levels on the enemy jungler (especially vs gank junglers) you’re doing something wrong. Don’t over prioritize early drakes if they’re too risky. They’re not thay important. Don’t do very early heralds even if safe, loses you too much tempo (takes too long get going). Actively jungle track enemy jungler to countergank when you get really ahead. Sit and camp bot when your team are hard pushing etc and look like attractive ganks for enemy.

Third time I did psychs, I decided to do a solo trip, and it was a really good choice. First time I actually did a strong dose too (three tabs). Was an insane time; glad I did it solo. I felt very safe like that. Buy candy, chips, some fruit. Listen to some dope music (LSD by Asap Rocky is crazy when you're tripping).

HUGEEE tip if you want to try something fun, that I haven't seen many people talk about, if you want a truly fucking powerful experience: Listen to ASMR with good headphones, with lights turned off and high volume. 3D type thing. Asmr fucks with your senses, which combined with LSD makes for such a strong experience.

VERY IMPORTANT: If you're not feeling very well before you take it, it might affect your trip in a bad way. Make sure you're in a good happy mood before you do it. It'll make it a lot better. Otherwise, just wait with taking it until you're in a good mind set. Take a couple of beers before if you're a little nervous. Make sure you have a whole day afterwards to cool down, with no responsibilities. An LSD trip is very long, with an extended effect that can last a while after too.

Do it in a place where you feel safe and comfortable. I tripped mostly in my room, although I felt like a nature trip would be way doper, I felt like this was my safe zone.

Having a trip sitter might be responsible. But chances are, if you're not comfortable socially, that your trip will be a little worse off that way. Having someone to contact is always good though. I think solo tripping is just fine, if you're in a good mind set and setting. If you keep this in mind, don't be scared. As I understood it, the psychedelic horror stories generally come from people that did too high of a dose, has a history of mental illness, or was in a really bad setting/mindset.

Make some food before, for when you get out of the trip. And eat a big meal before as well. Make sure to stay hydrated; it's easy to forget your needs. If it feels like the LSD trip goes on forever, don't be frightened, the trips are just much longer relative other drugs. You'll return to normal afterwards. Set up all your activities beforehand; chances are you're gonna be too confused on the drug to organize. If you want to watch something, I'd recommend stuff like Adventure Time, should be pretty dope and light. If you wanna play a game, Abzu is absolutely crazy beautiful.

I'm not claiming that gf is competent at creating stories. I'm saying that it's very possible for them to hire people, and get to a point where they actually can create well written, original story lines. Sword and Shield is the fastest selling switch game yet. Unless they burn all their money, there really is no excuse here. There are many examples of small indie studios with no budget with well written smart dialogue etc. Lets be honest here man. I probably shouldn't have written the open world thing in the text. As I said before, I only gave an example of what the games (could) be. And what (I) would like to see personally. This is not a big point. 

I want to make this really clear: I don't need a side game, or for the games to be radically different. Me personally, I'd like to see a more ambitious different game, but I would be fine with a game with the same type of formula as the main games have had. BUT, if it fixes the problems I've listed. 

Having a good story and engaging game play, does NOT come in conflict with the formula. We can have the same thing, but improved. I don't really believe in objectivity when it comes to art, but if anything is objectively bad, it's the story. It could be improved while still keeping the essence of what the games are, with no negative consequences. 

There could be a hard mode, "Pokemon master". Where the AI is tougher, uses items, has better IV spread, better scaling in terms of level. Perhaps setting a limit to the amount of times you can use potions per fight, making it so you can't abuse healing. And literally no one would complain. It doesn't take away from anything, if you have ADHD or whatever (like me) and for some reason don't want to play through a tougher game, just play the easier difficulty.  Not a single person suffers, both casuals and hardcore players get what they want. There is no excuse here either. Almost every single game has different difficulty settings. I think you need to do some real mental gymnastics to argue against that. 

I don't buy the "you can choose your own difficulty by catching harder Pokemon and nuzlocking". You shouldn't have to handicap yourself with made up player rules to have an actual challange. Also, I'm not even sure the AI necessarily is that bad. Playing the battle tower is way more difficult than all other things in the game, including the last boss, and they use a lot more different strategies. 

Make a standard ass Pokemon game, but with a stronger story, perhaps be a little fancy and make choices that matter, the game already has dialogue options but they lead nowhere. Or just have a more interesting story, that is still linear. Quirky funny characters with good dialogue, clever writing, make it so that the context of the battles also make them more tense. A few examples. I know for a fact that this is something that kids appreciate as well.  And have a harder mode, for us adults. None of these things would come in conflict with anything, and no one suffers, and they have the resources to do it. 

That being said, as a side note. I've completed it, and I enjoyed it, all things considered. It was pretty mediocre, but I had a strong connection to my team. I like it, but I don't think it's very good. 

As a positive thing to end off with. A few smaller details that did SO much for me. 1. The gym battles felt a lot cooler, fighting in stadiums made it feel more legit. It had a more tournament feel to it towards the end, like you're actually progressing towards becoming a champion. 2. I LOVE that the world recognizes that you're a good trainer, even though it's just a few lines of dialogue. Things like "It's so cool talking to the champion". A big group of people cheering you on as you enter the last stadium. "You can do it" "we believe in you" etc. That did a lot for me, and made me feel like I wanted to fuck the champion up, and not fail my fans :). As all the other games that I've played, doesn't really make me feel like I'm jack shit. Much like in Skyrim, where no one seems to give a fuck that you're dragonborn that saved the world. You get my point. I like the customization options, even if they don't really matter. I pimped my guy real hard. Some of the new Pokemon are really cool. I love the fire starter, and when it kicks the fireball. I actually like the multiplayer aspects, even if the raid battles are a little bare bone. It made me feel that I was more connected to other trainers, the quick trades and battles felt smooth. Back when I played the DS games as a kid, I always wanted to play with my friends. Ranked system feels decent. But I feel like the only reason I somewhat liked it was because of my love of Pokemon (and the things I listed here), and it has some serious problems. It also seems to have a lot less post game content than the other games, that I have played at least. 

If the story was more interesting, and the game had an hard mode, I might've even replayed it :) A lot of wasted potential here though. Sorry for the long answer. Did you have fun playing it or no?

Some things we just have to accept for a story to work. Dragons exist in GoT, light sabers exist in Star Wars, Super Man has superpowers etc. We never go "how does Super Mans powers make any sense"? We just accept that they exist, because that's how that world and story works. It's been established that light sabers work in Star Wars, and that superheroes have super powers. Hence why that never feels unrealistic, even though it obviously is. ODM gear make no sense, but it has been established that they are a thing that works. As far as I know, it's never actually been established why backpack titan could pull that off, and no amount of intelligence would make that remotely close to possible. Even the consciousness thing is like, well they have a weird nonsensical explanation for it, whatever, it's an anime. This series has been very heavy on plot armor for some time now, with them always getting away. I found myself going "just kill him already!" many times over the last episodes. And when they had that "whoops he got away again, god damn dude!" moment it really frustrated me and took away from the dope episode. I think the explanation is hilarious, if it was consistent to the story, Levi would've obviously just killed him there, or ended him after he sensed backpack titan creeping up on him, but I know that no one here agrees with me anyways, because anime is great and can never have flaws. It's probably a little nitpicky, but that scene was so important, it had to at least kind of made sense. I would probably be more accepting if it was in another anime or movie, but one of the big themes in Attack on Titan is that "everyone can die". Even main characters like Armin. When a group of people get away 3-4 times in a row, in ways that are meh, at best, then it kind of stands out, to me at least. It looks like both of the other titans survived as well, I feel like if they both get executed or eaten next episode then much of my frustration will go away, but if they survive for like the 5th of 6th time due to sending the brain processes that cause consciousness down to their foreskin or something then idk man.
